_why: tests/backend/test_panel_variant_name_codon_consistency.py decides which panel labels are accepted by asking whether a base substitution can produce a declared amino-acid change. That decision rests on the genetic code, which is a biological fact and must not be encoded from memory. This fixture is a verbatim transcription of NCBI translation table 1 - including its own Base1/Base2/Base3 codon-order lines, so even the codon ordering comes from the source rather than from an assumption - and the guard derives its codon table from here.
name: Standard
_transcription_sha256_note: SHA-256 over 'ncbieaa|sncbieaa|base1|base2|base3' as transcribed from NCBI gc.prt on 2026-08-10. Pinned because the genetic code is redundant: corrupting one codon of a multi-codon amino acid changes no reachability result and so is invisible to every other check here. Regenerate deliberately, and only when NCBI publishes a new table version.
